Subject: Intermittent packet truncation across private link (Stonebridge -> Redwood VPC)

Hi Sean,

We started seeing intermittent application errors when our backup appliance (on-prem) sends large 1500B UDP/HTTPS payloads to the Redwood private frontdoor in us-west-2. The app's retry logic triggers around 75-90s into the stream and we see TCP retransmits and truncated payloads. When we reduce MTU on the appliance to 1400 the problem disappears.

Prelim checks:
- Traceroute from our egress -> shows expected BGP path to Equinix colocation then transit into your VPC.
- No security group changes on our side in last 48h.
- ENIs show consistent Rx/Tx counters.

I'm attaching a short pcap from a failing flow + a trace. Can you confirm whether there's any MTU clamping or SNAT behavior on your private link that would cause fragmentation to be dropped? Also wondering if the GWLb or any intermediate NAT on Redwood's deployment is rewriting MSS.

Thanks,
Alan

Initial read: the symptom (disappears with lower MTU) strongly suggests either (1) an intermediate device dropping fragmented packets/ICMP 'fragmentation needed' being filtered, or (2) SNAT/MSS rewrite that forces larger segments through a path that can't handle them.

Quick asks so we can triage before we escalate to infra:

Sean/Team — I've pulled the pcap (stonebridge-pkts-20260731.pcap). Observations:
- The client sends large initial segments (MSS ~1460) and we see a sequence of ICMP fragmentation-needed messages originating from our edge IP but they are being rate-limited and, in a couple of flows, never reach the on-prem appliance.
- Edge logs show SNATing to a private gateway IP (203.0.113.45) as part of our transient egress path during a prior maintenance window. That SNAT IP sits behind a GWLb cluster configured for proxying TLS for private frontdoors.
- There are a handful of flows showing TCP RSTs right after a path MTU discovery attempt.

Hypothesis: after the maintenance change the SNAT hop introduced an MTU mismatch (jumbo offload / offpath fragmentation) and our edge is rate-limiting ICMP, so on-prem never gets the ICMP 'need frag' to adjust MSS.

Action items I'm starting now:
1) Dump SNAT policy and per-host offload settings for the 203.0.113.45 host.
2) Temporarily enable ICMP unreachable forwarding for the session path for Stonebridge (short window) so their appliance can see PMTUD messages.
3) Ask Equinix to confirm no ACLs are discarding fragmented packets at colo.

Alan, I'll post a short play-by-play — please hold any firewall changes; our change to ICMP forwarding will be narrow and logged.

-M

On Sat, Aug 1, 2026 at 08:15am, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Edge logs show SNATing to a private gateway IP (203.0.113.45) as part of our transient egress path during a prior maintenance window.

Quick update from the runtime/edge side after policy dump:
- SNAT policy: we had a fallback rule that rewrote source for flows matched to the private-handoff cluster during the maintenance window. The fallback rule did not include MSS clamping, and the host (203.0.113.45) had NIC offload settings that allowed 9000-byte frames to the local switch. On the path to Stonebridge there is a legacy MPLS hop that enforces a 1500 MTU and drops fragments.
- I pushed a targeted policy change: ensure SNAT translation now includes MSS clamp to 1380 for the private-handoff pool + disable TSO/GSO for that specific SNAT host to avoid large offloaded segments. This is active now and logged as change CHG-PL-3421.

Alan — can you please test the original workflow (without changing your appliance MTU) and confirm behavior? Also attaching a sanitized SNAT policy dump (snat-policy-dump-20260801.tar.gz).

Kimberly

Thanks Kimberly — confirmed. We re-ran the backup appliance job against the private frontdoor (no MTU change on our appliance) and the failure stopped. I can see the ICMP frag-needed messages now on our side and the retransmit rate has dropped to normal.

A few notes/questions for the postmortem:
- Would be great to document the SNAT fallback rule and conditions (CHG-PL-3421) so our ops team understands when they'll hit the SNAT host vs direct path.
- Can Redwood add the MSS clamp to the default private-handoff profile instead of only as an emergency change? That would prevent similar breakages during future maintenance windows.
- Can Equinix confirm there are no middlebox ACLs that would silently drop fragments in other colo regions?

Appreciate the quick response — feel free to close once the change is made persistent and the policy notes are updated in the drive link.

Alan
